prompt:
Warm editorial ink-and-wash illustration on a warm cream ground: a loose confident ink line with soft transparent washes over it, muted earth palette of cream, rust, ochre, mustard, sage and warm grey, quiet and hand-made, the register of a good picture book rather than a comic. Character reference: MIRA, a girl of about TEN. Dark hair in a blunt CHIN-LENGTH BOB with a straight fringe across her forehead. A MUSTARD-YELLOW KNITTED CARDIGAN with the sleeves pushed up, worn over a plain RUST-RED DRESS. Bare knees. Scuffed CREAM CANVAS SHOES. She stands in a relaxed neutral pose, FULL BODY visible head to feet, front three-quarter view, arms loose at her sides, looking calmly toward the viewer. She is an ORDINARY CHILD: absorbed, a little stubborn, slightly untidy. She is NOT precocious, NOT a tiny adult, NOT posed like a mascot, NOT grinning at the camera. Plain empty cream background with no scenery and no props. Render ONE single image only. This is NOT a contact sheet, NOT a grid, NOT a multi-panel study sheet, NOT a turnaround strip. No panel borders, no captions, no labels, no annotation text of any kind. ABSOLUTELY NOT, these are the rejected poles of this style and any of them is a failure: neon, 3D or CGI or Pixar rendering, glossy plastic, HUD or arc-reactor comic vocabulary, neo-comic styling, photorealism, airbrushing, lens flare, heavy drop shadows.

READABLE SURFACES FACE THEIR READER: any book, page, letter, scroll or sign a character is reading or writing faces THAT CHARACTER, never the camera. Compose over-the-shoulder or from behind so the surface genuinely faces them. Any handwriting is abstract handwriting-like line work with NO real readable letters.

NO USER INTERFACE ANYWHERE: no windows, menu bars, buttons, icons, toolbars, panels, form fields, cursors, floating rectangles or screenshot-like elements. Screens carry only soft glow or vague painterly shapes.
